text: Mesophilic lactococci turn part of the lactose into lactic acid, and the falling pH makes the casein clump into a soft gel. The diacetylactis strains and Leuconostoc add CO₂ and diacetyl, which give the buttery, fresh aroma. Raw milk left to sour by itself does the same with its own wild lactic bacteria, and no culture is added.
